Now let me reconsider whether there's an issue with `_linprog` trying multiple methods for infeasible lines. For an infeasible problem, 'highs-ds' returns status 2, then 'highs' (which chooses ds or ipm) might return status 2 too, then 'highs-ipm' status 2. Then we set seen_infeasible and return. But what if one method returns status 4 (numerical) after another returned 2? Our loop: best updated; if status 2 seen_infeasible True; if later status 4, we don't reset seen_infeasible. At end return best (which might be the status 4 result if it was last and we set best=res only when best is None or status2). Actually we set best=res only at first (best None) and when status2. So best stays a status2 result. Good. Return cls='infeasible'.

But there's a scenario: a feasible problem where 'highs-ds' returns status 4 (fails), 'highs' returns 0 -> we return optimal. Good. Or a feasible problem where all return 4 -> cls unknown -> we try farkas which would be infeasible (status 2) -> fres not optimal -> then last resort dual_lp on res.x (if res not None but status 4, res.x maybe None) -> fails -> returns invalid.
